name: What should be included in a custom home builder contract in LA?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a custom home builder contract in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a custom home builder contract in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom home builder contract in Los Angeles should do more than state the total price. It should clearly define the scope of work, what drawings and specifications are included, allowances for finishes, payment milestones, change order procedures, schedule assumptions, permit responsibilities, insurance requirements, warranty coverage, and exactly what is excluded. It should also identify who manages subcontractors, inspections, debris removal, protection of neighboring property, and site security. Homeowners should look closely at allowances because a low allowance can make a bid look cheaper than it really is. The contract should also explain how delays are handled, especially for weather, permitting, or material lead times. If the project is on a hillside or in a dense neighborhood, the builder should specify how access, parking, staging, and utility shutdowns will be managed. A good contract reduces conflict by making expectations measurable before work begins. If important items are vague or missing, the homeowner should have them clarified before signing.
acceptedAnswer.description: A custom home builder contract should clearly define scope, plans, allowances, payment schedule, change order rules, timeline, warranties, insurance, permit responsibilities, and exclusions. It should also specify who handles subs, inspections, site protection, and cleanup so there is no confusion during the build.
